answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil attacks are resisted by forcing every new identity to stake a unique non-reusable bond called an echo that is permanently burned upon detection of duplication. The bond is tied to a challenge quill generated from a continuous river of prior network proofs, so each fake identity demands independent computational effort that cannot be amortized. This makes large-scale faking expensive because the attacker loses the full bond value plus compute for every additional identity created.
